A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable versions of the same Feature Tuning Mixup paper. Their methods, equations, experiments, figures, and supplementary material can be reliably matched, including relocated tables.

before.justification: v1 reports original targeted-attack success rates, computational timings, ablations, and adversarial examples on the ImageNet-compatible dataset, including supplementary experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds clean-accuracy measurements, multimodal-language-model attack outcomes, and ViT-surrogate results.

M1.justification: The core FTM objective and feature-update equations remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 revises input transformation from assigning phi(x_adv) to x_adv to evaluating F(phi(x_adv)). Appendix A.4 adds a specific FTM-E/SI variant that assigns input scales 1 and 0.5 to the two surrogate copies.

E1.justification: Appendix A.2 expands evaluation from image classifiers to prompted multimodal language models: Qwen2-VL, Llama-3.2, Claude-3.5, and GPT-4o. Although images still come from the ImageNet-compatible dataset, this introduces a distinct language-conditioned image-recognition scenario with yes/no responses, refusals, and uncertain answers.

E2.justification: The RN-50+Inc-v3 comparison adds RDI-ODI-CFM, RDI-Admix-CFM, and RDI-SI-CFM in v2 Table 3, absent from the corresponding v1 Table 5 experiment. The single-RN-50 combination comparison, including VT combinations, is removed. The main comparator sets in Tables 1–2 remain unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 introduces a protocol using 100 randomly selected images, ViT-generated attacks, and a target-label yes/no prompt for multimodal models. It also adds ViT-surrogate experiments. Table 3 changes from a single RN-50 surrogate to RN-50+Inc-v3, an ensemble already evaluated elsewhere in v1. The standard 300 iterations, perturbation budget, and step size remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Table 4 measures surrogate clean accuracy across p=0.1–1.0 with and without clean feature mixup, extending the existing attack-success sensitivity analysis in Figure 6. This directly investigates the high-p failure mechanism. The earlier parameter sweeps, ensemble analysis, and adversarial-example visualizations are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or error bars. The 'Uncertain' responses in v2 Table 5 classify language-model answers and do not constitute statistical uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 and the earlier supplementary Tables 4–5 retain their numerical results; the latter become Tables 6–7. v2 removes the single-RN-50 combination results and expands ensemble comparisons with additional scores and timings. New results include the clean-accuracy sweep, 40.5% average reported multimodal attack success, and ViT-surrogate scores and timings in Tables 8–9. These are additions under new settings, not same-setting performance improvements.

T1.justification: The mathematical assumptions, minimax formulation, and Equations (1)–(15) retain their substance. The added efficiency discussion is informal reasoning rather than a new formal definition, theorem, proof, or derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: optimized feature perturbations and stochastic updates improve targeted transferability efficiently, with further benefits from surrogate ensembles. The supplementary additions do not redefine these core contributions.

C2.justification: Section 4.3 and Appendix A.1 now attribute the high-p attack collapse to degraded surrogate clean accuracy: 3.8% with clean feature mixup versus 65.3% without it at p=1. v2 also adds architecture-related efficiency reasoning and explains shallow-layer exclusion through sensitivity to input transformations.

D1.justification: v2 adds a first-page code-availability statement and repository URL. It also specifies fully connected layer outputs for pure-ViT perturbation, the two input scales used in the added FTM-E/SI variant, and the multimodal evaluation prompt. These provide additional implementation and access information.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to UV-attack and Wang et al.'s Towards Transferable Targeted Adversarial Examples, and refines the introductory categorization of related attacks. Its central positioning relative to CFM, intermediate-level attacks, and adversarial-learning methods remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The main narrative receives localized wording edits and additional explanatory paragraphs. Supplementary Section 6 becomes Appendix A with five subsections and an introductory roadmap. Author contact information and acknowledgments are expanded, while the main section sequence and most prose remain intact.

P2.justification: The experimental presentation is substantially reorganized: Table 2 becomes single-column, Table 3 is rebuilt, four new tables are introduced, and the two retained supplementary tables are consolidated onto one page. Timing columns are reorganized, Figure 3 moves, Figure 2 gains mathematical annotations, and Figure 6's caption expands. Figures 7–8 remain identical.

improvement.justification: The clean-accuracy analysis strengthens the explanation of a failure case, the ViT experiments support architectural efficiency, and the code-access information improves reproducibility documentation. These are useful gains beyond the unchanged core results. Their overall benefit is limited by removal of the earlier single-RN-50 combination comparison and the new multimodal test's lack of clean-image controls or competing attack baselines.
